beats.heading: News carries a version, never the board

beats.heading: The socket owns screen presence
beats.body: Only the authoritative socket owns a pane identity. Its close removes pane and tab presence; a replaced socket cannot retire its successor.

beats.heading: News carries a version, never the board
beats.body: A board write, claim or disk change reaches the panes through announcements. The pane reads content again from the store; no pane owns a board copy.

beats.heading: Agents read the same news
beats.body: The change feed records each board broadcast and lets the workbench read changes since its cursor. Tab presence allows a reload to keep its conversation.

beats.heading: The server decides which vault a pane is in
beats.body: A show that names a pane, or a new chosen checkout of the repository it shows, moves the pane into another vault. The pane only mirrors that: it takes the vault from pane_board and names it on its socket, reports and calls. A report that names the vault it left is answered as not registered, so it cannot undo the move.

beats.heading: The socket owns screen presence

beats.heading: News carries a version, never the board

beats.heading: Agents read the same news

beats.heading: A change on disk is announced like a write
beats.body: One vault can be open in more than one server, so a write from another process reaches no pane through this server's broadcast. The lock sweep compares each board on screen with the fingerprint it last saw, and a difference is announced as a change with no version. The pane answers by reading the board again.

Explanation invocation opens the existing session for a registered tab and uses its checkout workhorse. Latest-action discovery starts no agent work.

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards, says what each pane is showing, and writes nothing

nodes.name: Pane routes
nodes.responsibility: What each pane shows and where, pushed by the browser, which answers a report naming a vault the pane left as not registered; the CLI opens, closes and shows panes through it

nodes.name: Pane socket
nodes.responsibility: One socket per page, named for its vault, or put in a readable one when that vault is gone: registers it, tells it its vault and repository, notes its tab, and passes agent messages to the workbench

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: Board announcements
nodes.responsibility: Tells every pane on a board of one vault who holds it and what they said they were doing, and every pane what agents are doing in each vault
nodes.description: ADR 0022: a claim is visible wherever the board is shown. Board content is never in the news; a pane reads the board again.

nodes.name: Change feed
nodes.responsibility: Every settled board change, filed under its vault, as one stream with a cursor, read off the panes' announcements, for the agent's context

nodes.name: Pane tab adapter
nodes.responsibility: Attach pane registration and browser conversation activation to the shared tab session owner
nodes.description: The Archboard adapter selects the initial checkout from pane focus and forwards registrations, shown-conversation reads, and browser activation to the core-owned tab store. The store outlives Codex child generations.

nodes.name: HTTP listener
nodes.responsibility: The one Express application and the HTTP server that answers for it

nodes.name: Server entry
nodes.responsibility: The process entry that archboard start spawns: it starts the server and reports a startup failure

nodes.name: Browser origin guard
nodes.responsibility: Checks browser request origins at HTTP and WebSocket entry points

nodes.name: Vault requirement
nodes.responsibility: Refuses a call or a socket that names no vault, or one the server cannot read, including a directory whose real path is not <dir>/.archboard/vault, and hands a route the canonical vault it named
nodes.description: ADR 0049: the socket names its vault once in its URL and the pane routes name it on every call. News of a board goes only to the panes of that board's vault.

nodes.name: Pane session
nodes.responsibility: One pane's contact with the server: holds the vault and repository the server put it in, and names that vault on its socket, reports, readings and calls
nodes.description: pane-arrival adopts the vault and repository that a pane_board message names, and pane-core keeps them as a mirror of the server. pane-socket opens the socket with ?vault= and socket-messages routes each message. A report is keyed by its vault, so the server answers one naming a vault the pane left with registered:false. Canonical reports preserve architecture metadata when the legacy board is null. The request names the admitted pane vault, while architecture names the actual reading vault. Explanation controls wait for pane registration. A tab-scoped explanation notice invalidates the existing answer query.

nodes.name: Repository routes
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories and chooses a checkout, and watches the registry file: each pane in an unchosen checkout's vault moves to the chosen one, and every pane hears its repository's name

nodes.name: Pane vaults
nodes.responsibility: Moves a pane into another vault, re-keying its sockets and registration and forgetting what it said it was reading, and broadcasts machine news to every tab
nodes.description: It tells nobody that a pane moved: which conversation the tab's agent dock shows stays as it is, because only the person's own act in the page changes that.

nodes.name: Repository list
nodes.responsibility: Names each vault the way the navigator lists it: a repository identity, or an untracked vault's registry name, read from the chosen checkout
nodes.description: A vault whose real path is not <dir>/.archboard/vault, such as one that a link leads out of the layout, is no vault here: its checkout reads no-vault, and an untracked one is not listed. A vault that no registry entry holds has no repository name. Every vault has a checkout, the directory that holds it, so a pane and a shown board always report one. No environment variable names a vault: the page opens in the first ready repository by name.

nodes.name: Panes report
nodes.responsibility: What every pane on screen shows, with the repository and checkout of its vault, and whether that is the vault of the caller's own checkout
nodes.description: Publishes accepted pane readings. Canonical walkthrough reports retain the actual vault, source selector, observed source and target revisions, and the current beat. Presentation arrival comes from the rendered scene and camera. The browser authors no architecture.

nodes.name: Shown conversation
nodes.responsibility: The person's own act in the page names the checkout whose conversation every pane of the tab shows; a pick of a checkout the tab does not work in is refused
nodes.description: The existing workbench showConversation operation validates a pane and its vault, resolves allowed checkouts, and changes the shown conversation. The server route delegates the complete request without assembling workbench internals.

nodes.name: Pane connections
nodes.responsibility: Accepts each page's socket and pane, keeps which pane shows what in which tab, reports what the panes show, and moves a pane to the checkout a person chooses

nodes.name: Board news
nodes.responsibility: Notices that a board changed and tells the panes of its vault, and files each change for the agent's context

nodes.name: Server plumbing
nodes.responsibility: Boots and stops the server, mounts every route, and holds each call to the vault it names

nodes.name: Board routes
nodes.responsibility: The routes that write, rename, move and show boards: each tells the panes what it did, and a show or a move takes panes to another vault

nodes.name: Semantic context input
nodes.responsibility: Reads each board a thread works on, with its claim, into the brief the agent is given
nodes.description: Accept ordered pane reports and notify the coordinator context source directly when canonical reading intent changes. Resolve explanation actions from that explicit canonical report, never from the initial legacy board.

nodes.name: Pane messages
nodes.responsibility: Applies server board and version messages to the pane

nodes.name: Shared tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: Own browser tab presence, disconnect grace, shown checkout, and session end notifications

nodes.name: Presentation position
nodes.responsibility: Reports arrived narrative beats and resolves existing presentation requests
nodes.description: Canonical and legacy panes use the same position contract and request acknowledgement. A missing beat never reports arrival. A recording advances its own beat and voice follows accepted positions.

beats.heading: The socket owns screen presence
beats.body: Only the authoritative socket owns a pane identity. Its close removes pane and tab presence; a replaced socket cannot retire its successor.

beats.heading: News carries a version, never the board
beats.body: A board write, claim or disk change reaches the panes through announcements. The pane reads content again from the store; no pane owns a board copy.

beats.heading: Agents read the same news
beats.body: The change feed records each board broadcast and lets the workbench read changes since its cursor. Tab presence allows a reload to keep its conversation.

beats.heading: A change on disk is announced like a write
beats.body: One vault can be open in more than one server, so a write from another process reaches no pane through this server's broadcast. The lock sweep compares each board on screen with the fingerprint it last saw, and a difference is announced as a change with no version. The pane answers by reading the board again.

beats.heading: The server decides which vault a pane is in
beats.body: A show that names a pane, or a new chosen checkout of the repository it shows, moves the pane into another vault. The pane only mirrors that: it takes the vault from pane_board and names it on its socket, reports and calls. A report that names the vault it left is answered as not registered, so it cannot undo the move.
